statement: For every (b, Z) ∈ D, the following conclusions hold. 1. The quotient j(b, Z) = − H′(−ib, 6, −iZ) H(−ib, 6, −iZ) is well defined and satisfies |j(b, Z)| < 3 · 10−9. It is nonzero on ∂D, and, identifying C with R2 in the order real part, imaginary part, deg(j, D, 0) = −1. 2. For every real z ≥ Z, H(−ib, 6, −iz) ̸= 0 and Re j(b, z) < .043. (2.3) For z ≥ 3 one also has Im j(b, z) > 0. 3. For ℓ ∈ {0, 1, 2, . . .} and h ∈ {1, −1} define qh = λ + ℓ/2 − hib, Jh(λ) = H(qh, 6 + ℓ, −hiZ) −H′(qh, 6 + ℓ, −hiZ) ! . (2.4) The columns Jh are holomorphic and nonzero on a neighborhood of Re λ ≥ −1/32. The determinant ∆ℓ(λ; b, Z) = det(J+(λ), J−(λ)) has no zero on Re λ = −1/32. In the closed half-plane Re λ ≥ −1/32 its numbers of zeros, counted with holomorphic multiplicity, are ℓ 0 1 ℓ ≥ 2 #{∆ℓ = 0} 2 1 0. The locations of the symmetry zeros are identified later at parameters where j(b, Z) = 0; the count in this proposition holds on the entire disk.
